#5269. Morning Minute: CFTC Clears Stock Perps, Gets Sued the Same Day

Morning Minute: CFTC Clears Stock Perps, Gets Sued the Same Day

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

⚖️ CFTC Clears Stock Perps, Gets Sued the Same Day

A perpetual future is a leveraged bet on a price that never expires. You hold it as long as you can meet margin and keep paying a funding rate. It’s analog product would be options in TradFi, with a few differences (primarily no expiration date). Crypto traders have used them for years, mostly on offshore venues like Binance and onchain platforms like Hyperliquid, because U.S. law had no clear home for the product.

On Tuesday the CFTC said Americans can now trade them on individual stocks.

Hours later, Wall Street sued to stop it.

The approval came as a statement from CFTC Chairman Michael Selig. Equity perpetual futures are now tradable on CFTC-registered exchanges, classified as security futures products under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000, which puts them under joint CFTC and SEC oversight.

The list of venues that can actually do this is short, and it was assembled quietly. A firm needs to be a CFTC-designated contract market and separately notice-registered with the SEC as a national securities exchange for security futures products. Seven entities hold both today: Cboe, CME, Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial, Nadex, and ICE Futures U.S. Five of those seven filed inside a single 30-day window in September.

Kalshi is furthest along, with a filing covering 56 to 58 names and a launch expected within days. Coinbase has filed to list perps on Apple, Tesla and Nvidia. So those two are immediate winners. But Hyperliquid and Lighter, the top crypto perps protocols, are next in line for potential CFTC approvals and are likely future winners as well (LIT +10% on the day).

Then came the lawsuit. A new group called the Capital Markets Alliance filed in the Southern District of New York, naming Cboe, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association among its members. Its argument runs on two tracks.

The group wants the policy eliminated. The American Securities Association piled on separately, pointing out that Congress banned selling security-based swaps to retail investors at all.

A CFTC spokesman called the suit “troubling,” adding that “our markets should be governed by law, not litigation campaigns intended to block innovation.” The CME already tried this once, suing over the CFTC’s crypto perps approval on the theory that perpetuals are swaps rather than futures. That one went nowhere.

Well, remember that old phrase: “First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you, then you win."

We’re at the fight stage. Next stop, winning.

#5267. 70.5 Million POL Heist Triggers Polygon’s Hard Fork Proposal

Home » Altcoins » 70.5 Million POL Heist Triggers Polygon’s Hard Fork Proposal

A controversial governance proposal requires a hard fork to retrieve the looted balance in two separate incidents.

Two previous hacking incidents on Polygon’s Proof Of Stake (PoS) chain have looted nearly 70.50 million tokens, worth approximately $6.5 million at the current rates. A fresh hard-fork proposal from a member of the Polygon Labs Validator Support Team is looking to retrieve the sum via new amendments.

The idea is to move them from the attackers’ addresses into recovery wallets designated and verified by Binance & Polymarket, the platforms where the Polygon (POL) related accidents took place. On 29th and 30th October 2026, Polymarket and Binance each dealt with separate POL-tied hacking instances.

The block-producing POL nodes are presently restricting these funds from traveling across the blockchain. However, if this Polygon (POL) dev proposal gets granted, an extreme measure is expected to be taken: the frozen funds are sent back to a recovery address that Polymarket & Binance designated & verified.

Polygon Labs Member Proposes Hard Fork to Recover Approximately 70.49 Million POL Stolen from Polymarket and BinanceA member of the Polygon Labs Validator Support Team has published a Polygon Improvement Proposal (PIP) suggesting a hard fork on the Polygon PoS mainnet to… pic.twitter.com/n8hoCCsYms

The 70.50 million proposal is scheduled for discussion during the Polygon Protocol Governance Call on November 5. If approved, developers expect to complete client development and testnet rehearsals within approximately two to three weeks. The proposal guarantees there’s not one new POL token created & supply stays fixed.

During the Polymarket-related incident on October 29, 2026, two malicious POL transfers were indicated, moving a combined 3,282,275.71 POL between addresses. The PoS network’s node validators managed to block four addresses containing roughly 24 million POL. This POL returning coordinated transfer needs to be done at a particular block size.

That’s what makes the Polygon developer (POL) offer rather difficult to carry out. Intriguingly,  the attacker also reportedly contacted validators and offered cash payments in exchange for help removing the restrictions. Whichever way this plays out, the proposal raises a crucial question about how far a decentralized network should go to recover stolen coins.

With cyberattacks getting more common, it’s important to implement procedures to retrieve the stolen funds along with precautionary steps to prevent cybercrime.

#5264. Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Cyberattack After ZachXBT Ties It to $133M Crypto Theft

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Cyberattack After ZachXBT Ties It to $133M Crypto Theft

French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa has confirmed that it was hit by a cyberattack that allowed fraudulent operations, a day after onchain investigator ZachXBT named it as the alleged victim of a crypto theft of more than $133 million.

In a statement shared with Decrypt on Wednesday, the bank said the incident was "closed and now under control," and that operations were resuming gradually after it put stronger security measures in place. It said customers' assets were not affected, and that the attack had only delayed the execution of some transfers.

The bank did not mention crypto or say how much was taken. The amounts affected are still being assessed, but are "in any event not of a nature to call into question the solidity and financial health of the group," it said, according to Decrypt's translation.

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said it informed the relevant supervisory authorities as soon as it detected the attack, and temporarily suspended some transactions as a precaution to prevent further fraudulent movements. It also warned customers to watch out for phishing attempts following the attack. Decrypt has reached out to Crédit Mutuel Arkéa for further comment, including on whether the losses involved crypto.

"Disclosing the EU financial institution exploited for $133M+ is allegedly Credit Mutuel Arkea, a French bank with $235B in assets," ZachXBT wrote on his Telegram channel on Tuesday. "The attack on the bank occurred for multiple days. I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity."

In an update on Tuesday, he said he had identified a further $27 million in exchange withdrawals by the attacker, bringing the total to more than $133 million, and that some of those withdrawals took place after his initial disclosure. He also published four Ethereum addresses he said were linked to the theft.

"My working theory is a large financial institution in Western Europe was exploited and it's currently being covered up," ZachXBT wrote at the time, accusing it of not having conducted "proper incident disclosure" and thereby preventing law enforcement from freezing some $30 million in stolen funds.

He did not say how he had identified the bank, or how the attacker gained access to its exchange accounts.

The mutual banking group has been preparing to move into crypto. In May, French financial newspaper L'Agefi reported that it had applied for a license under MiCA, the EU's crypto rulebook, to offer crypto services to its retail customers and to provide them as a white-label service through its Arkéa Banking Services division.

The allegation comes days after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the largest crypto theft on record, which the FBI has attributed to North Korean hackers. ZachXBT said the attacker in the suspected EU theft remains unidentified, but that he could say "with a high degree of confidence it is NOT Lazarus Group," the North Korean hacking collective, "based on multiple laundering indicators."

This story has been updated to add comment from Crédit Mutuel Arkéa.

#5263. Gate Pioneers Proof of Security (PoSEC), Achieving 104.58% Cold Storage Coverage to Solidify Asset Security

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Gate has officially introduced Proof of Security (PoSEC), a new asset security verification framework, becoming the first digital asset trading platform in the industry to launch a PoSEC security verification system. Since its founding in 2013, Gate has consistently placed user asset security at the forefront of its priorities. With the introduction of PoSEC, Gate extends security verification beyond reserve adequacy to include asset storage structures and risk coverage capabilities, further solidifying safeguards for user assets and providing a new practical approach to advancing industry security standards.

Unlike Proof of Reserves (PoR), which primarily verifies the adequacy of asset reserves, PoSEC places additional emphasis on asset storage security. By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios.

PoSEC introduces the cold storage coverage ratio as a key metric to measure the extent to which cold storage covers total user assets. A coverage ratio ≥ 100% means that, under the applicable calculation methodology, cold storage alone would be sufficient to cover all user assets even if all assets held in hot wallets were lost. PoR and PoSEC serve complementary purposes, extending asset security verification from reserve adequacy to storage security and risk coverage, while providing users with more comprehensive and transparent information about asset security.

According to the snapshot taken at 00:00 (UTC) on November 4, 2026, Gate’s cold storage coverage ratio reached 104.58%, with cold storage and hot wallet assets accounting for 88.26% and 11.74% of total assets, respectively. Cold storage assets include digital assets held offline and traditional assets under independent custody. To qualify, these assets must meet requirements such as not being directly used for routine deposits and withdrawals, being held offline or under independent custody, requiring multi-party authorization for transfers, and being independently verifiable.

The current data is undergoing verification by an independent third-party audit firm. The review covers asset authenticity and control, valuation and calculation methodologies, and coverage ratio calculations. The audit report will be published on Gate’s official website upon completion, enhancing the transparency and credibility of asset security disclosures.

Gate has long been committed to digital asset security and transparency. In 2020, Gate was among the first in the industry to introduce an open-source Proof of Reserves (PoR) mechanism and a Merkle Tree-based asset verification solution, establishing itself as an early contributor to reserve transparency in the industry. Gate subsequently incorporated technologies such as zk-SNARKs to enhance its asset reserve verification framework.

As of October 18, 2026, Gate’s total reserves amounted to approximately $8.688 billion, with an overall reserve ratio of 118.49%. The platform also employs a range of security mechanisms, including hot and cold wallet segregation, multi-signature technology, Multi-Party Computation (MPC), dynamic risk monitoring, and zero-trust access control, to establish a multi-layered security framework covering asset reserves, storage management, and risk protection.

From PoR, which verifies reserve adequacy, to PoSEC, which verifies asset storage security and risk coverage capabilities, Gate is progressively building a multi-layered security framework encompassing asset reserves, storage management, risk protection, and public verification. Looking ahead, Gate will continue to uphold its security-first principle, further develop PoSEC standards and verification mechanisms, and collaborate with more industry participants to enhance asset security and transparency, laying a stronger security foundation for the long-term, sustainable development of the digital asset industry.

Learn more: https://www.gate.com/proof-of-security

#5262. XRP Ledger: Ripple Boasts Up to 23% Drop in Node Memory Use

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The XRP Ledger continues to evolve with node memory usage reduced by up to 23% since the release of xrpld version 3.3.0. The release included several new amendments, as well as bug fixes and build improvements in August 2026.

RippleX developer Valentin Balaschenko shares a deep dive on how the memory consumption decline was achieved in an official blog post.

Memory growth in XRPL nodes was observed in late summer 2025. Operators reported increasing memory usage on their validators that did not decrease, including on nodes configured identically to others that were unaffected, and across different hardware platforms. The cause turned out not to be a memory leak but the memory allocator retaining memory the application had already freed, and a fix was shipped in xrpld 3.3.0.

A memory regression identified in one release during that period was addressed within weeks, but this had no observable impact for operators. The observed memory behavior existed before the regression and persisted after the fix. The underlying issue remained unresolved at the time. Operators monitoring node caches asked why memory did not come back after a cache sweep, the routine pass that clears expired entries.

Hussein Zangana (Vet), XRP Ledger Foundation director of community, mentioned this development in an X post: "Up to 23% memory savings on XRP Ledger nodes since 3.3.0. Given how expensive RAM is at the moment, this improvement is especially useful. Measured on (non/dUNL) validators as well as stock nodes, savings range from 13-23% depending on history."

The fixCleanup amendment was activated on the XRP Ledger this week on November 4, 2026, hardening and improving the XRP protocol.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation.

The fix upgrade changes VaultClawback to reject pseudo-account holders and updates VaultDeposit, VaultWithdraw, and VaultClawback to round more precisely, so vault assets can't over- or under-deliver. It changes VaultWithdraw to allow a fixed-share withdrawal to move zero assets from a fully impaired vault rather than failing. It also exempts an IOU issuer from their own global freeze on NFT offers in their own currency.

Start with one stock. Connect two capital worlds.

6 November — Singapore — StockFi is advancing the connection between traditional equities and the on-chain ecosystem through U.S. stock tokenization. Built on BSC, the platform brings stock tokens and the meme ecosystem into its development strategy, exploring new ways to serve on-chain users worldwide through asset issuance, on-chain circulation and product applications.

StockFi’s approach connects the underlying value of equities, the utility of on-chain products and the reach of communities. Starting with its first stock offering, the platform plans to progressively develop asset onboarding, token issuance, trading environments and user access, giving equities broader reach and utility once they enter the on-chain market.

“Start with one stock. Connect two capital worlds.” This brand statement reflects StockFi’s understanding of asset tokenization: begin with a specific asset, connect markets through products, and support ecosystem development through sustained use.

Equities connect business operations with capital markets, reflecting investors’ assessments of industry development, commercial innovation and long-term value. On-chain networks offer a new digital environment in which assets can connect with users and products across regions through wallets, trading protocols and application interfaces.

When equities enter the on-chain market as tokens, the change extends beyond how assets are represented. It also affects how they are discovered, how they circulate, and how they connect with other digital assets and applications.

StockFi will focus its development on these areas.

Within the platform’s roadmap, equities and on-chain products require clearly defined structural connections. Products and users need convenient access points, while assets entering the market require appropriate liquidity and application support. Bringing these elements together is essential to delivering a complete asset tokenization experience.

Through ongoing product development, StockFi aims to combine the market familiarity of traditional equities with the open connectivity of the on-chain ecosystem, creating new opportunities for collaboration among asset issuers, ecosystem partners and eligible users.

StockFi’s product framework encompasses real stocks, stock tokens and MEME tokens. Each serves a distinct role in connecting assets with communities.

Real stocks form the underlying asset foundation, connecting company operations with traditional capital markets. Stock tokens provide the corresponding on-chain representation, serving as a product vehicle for trading, asset information and future applications. MEME tokens connect community culture, content distribution and user participation, helping the platform broaden its market reach.

This structure allows StockFi to develop both the asset and user sides of the platform.

On the asset side, key questions include where products originate, how they are issued and what rights holders receive. On the user side, participants need to understand a product’s purpose, find an access point and build familiarity through actual use. StockFi plans to bring these two sides closer together through an integrated platform experience.

The asset characteristics, uses and holder rights of stock tokens and MEME tokens will be explained separately. Their connections will take shape through trading environments, product integration and community participation, providing complementary foundations for platform development.

Communities are an important part of on-chain markets. Content, discussion and creative work built around shared themes help projects reach across regions and languages to establish distinctive brand cultures.

StockFi views the meme ecosystem as an important gateway to users and aims to bring community reach into the stock token experience.

Under its development plans, StockFi will select eligible projects from a pool of candidate MEME projects, work toward establishing trading pairs with stock tokens, and provide educational content and product introductions around specific assets. This approach can introduce community users to stock tokens while helping stock tokens attract broader attention and potential demand.

These connections require ongoing support from both content and products. After discovering an asset theme, users should be able to learn more about its background, structure and purpose. Once they access the product, they should also find clear information and operating instructions.

StockFi will therefore develop its community alongside its products. Through accurate asset introductions, accessible educational content and ongoing ecosystem engagement, the platform aims to turn brand awareness into product understanding and establish a foundation for long-term use.

StockFi sees asset issuance as the starting point of its platform services, with subsequent circulation and applications remaining central to its ongoing development.

For stock tokens, the platform plans to progressively connect asset arrangements, issuance services, on-chain trading and DApp access. These capabilities will be introduced in stages according to product delivery and partnership progress, creating a continuous path from asset information to practical use.

At the asset onboarding stage, the platform plans to work with relevant service providers on stock sourcing, custody and issuance structures, while clearly defining product information and holder rights.

For on-chain circulation, StockFi plans to develop stock token trading environments and connect wallets and liquidity services, providing product support for assets entering the on-chain market.

For the user experience, the platform will integrate asset displays, project materials and feature access through its DApp, helping users learn about assets, review information and access available services within a single product environment.

Together, these elements define StockFi’s product direction: make assets identifiable, information understandable and services usable. As its capabilities develop, the platform will further explore how stock tokens can be used across different on-chain applications.

Bringing equities into the on-chain market requires expertise from multiple fields. Asset services, technical development, wallet integration, liquidity and user education each play an essential role along the product journey.

StockFi will expand ecosystem partnerships around specific product needs, enabling partners to collaborate within clearly defined service scopes and delivery requirements.

For asset and issuance service partners, priorities will include asset selection, asset arrangements, custody, issuance and ongoing disclosure, establishing a clear product foundation for stock tokens.

For technology, wallet and liquidity partners, the platform will explore asset displays, trading access and application integrations to progressively improve how stock tokens are accessed and used.

For media and community partners, StockFi will provide consistent brand introductions, project materials and educational content, helping more users understand stock tokenization and the platform’s direction through ongoing communication.

StockFi aims to build an ecosystem in which every partnership serves a specific product need and every asset onboarded receives appropriate application support. As its network of partners and product use cases grows, the platform will progressively expand its ability to connect assets with users.

StockFi plans to begin with its first stock offering, connecting assets, issuance, circulation and user access, then refining the product journey based on actual operation.

The first offering will establish a reusable foundation for future development. Practical questions—how asset information is presented, how stock tokens enter trading environments, and how users understand and use products—will inform the platform’s subsequent expansion.

Building on this foundation, StockFi will consider product delivery, market demand and partnership progress as it explores onboarding additional stock tokens and eligible MEME projects, broadening its asset coverage and application range.

The platform’s long-term goal is to establish lasting connections among asset supply, product use and community participation: more products give users greater choice, more use cases support asset demand, and broader community reach contributes to ecosystem development.

Starting with one stock, StockFi aims to establish a product pathway into the on-chain market, creating a new connection between traditional equities and the global on-chain ecosystem.

#5258. Bitcoin Tumbles to $75K as AI Fears Wipe $150B From Crypto

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Tumbles to $75K as AI Fears Wipe $150B From Crypto

Massive liquidations shake digital assets as growing fears over AI spending ripple through global markets.

Bitcoin fell to $75,350 on November 6 as a broader crypto market sell-off wiped nearly $150 billion from the digital asset market in 24 hours.

The sharp downturn came as crypto assets tracked a broader retreat from risk assets, sparked by concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending that triggered a major Wall Street sell-off.

According to CoinGecko, total crypto market capitalization declined by more than 5.1%, while leveraged traders faced $1.25 billion in liquidations, piling further pressure onto already falling prices.

Ethereum fell 7.9%, XRP dropped 8.7% and Solana declined 6.4% over the same period, per CoinGecko data. The crypto market sell-off followed a sharp decline in US technology stocks on Thursday.

The November 5 rout wiped roughly $2.5 trillion from US stock market value. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.52%, marking its worst trading session since April 2025 and pushing the index more than 10% below its October 6 record high.

The S&P 500 and the Dow also posted their worst sessions since then.

Investor concerns grew that Democratic gains in the US midterms could slow AI infrastructure expansion, particularly in Texas. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa proposed pausing new data center construction until stronger protections are introduced, raising uncertainty over major investments by Google, Meta, Oracle and OpenAI.

AI and semiconductor stocks weakened ahead of Thursday’s broader sell-off. On Friday, November 6, South Korea’s Kospi plunged nearly 9% at the open, triggering a 20-minute trading halt.

Nevertheless, some experts suggest that the AI stock sell-off could ultimately benefit the health of the market.

Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, told CNN that slowing AI infrastructure investment could help cool an increasingly speculative market.

“We want a slowdown in the AI buildout. It was too frenzied and speculative,” Yardeni said, adding that allowing air to escape the AI bubble gradually would be preferable to an abrupt collapse.

Concerns about excessive data center construction have also intensified as investors question whether future demand will justify the industry’s aggressive infrastructure spending.

Meanwhile, demand for government bonds increased during the sell-off, pushing the 10-year US Treasury yield down to 4.84%, its lowest level in two months.

Bitcoin and altcoins are trading in step with tech stocks, so equity-market shocks can quickly hit crypto prices. Heavy long liquidations show how leverage can amplify downside moves.

#5256. Wall Street’s Plumbing Goes Onchain as Morgan Stanley Tokenizes Securities

Wall Street’s Plumbing Goes Onchain as Morgan Stanley Tokenizes Securities

Morgan Stanley has started moving U.S. stocks and Treasuries onto blockchain rails, using Wall Street’s own plumbing to do it.

The bank said Tuesday that it’s among the first to tokenize real-world assets through the DTCC Tokenization Service, converting U.S. equities and Treasuries into tokenized form.

The service, which went live Oct. 28, is run by the Depository Trust Co., a subsidiary of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp. The DTC is the post-trade backbone of U.S. markets, with more than $114 trillion in assets under custody.

“The hands-on experience of integrating tokenized securities with established market infrastructure will inform the continued development of the firm’s digital asset capabilities as the market evolves,” said Amy Oldenburg, Morgan Stanley’s head of digital assets strategy.

The service lets eligible firms convert securities held at DTC into tokenized “digital twins” and back again, delivering them to digital wallets of their choice. The tokens keep the same ownership rights, investor protections and economic entitlements as the originals, according to DTCC, and are designed to let firms move collateral and tap new pools of liquidity within minutes. The service currently runs on the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network, with more blockchains planned for 2027.

Morgan Stanley is one of 20 DTC participants that have signed up so far, alongside Bank of America, Citi, J.P. Morgan, Fidelity Investments, Citadel Securities, and UBS, among others. DTCC said it developed the service with input from more than 150 firms.

The launch caps a regulatory path that began in December 2025, when the SEC gave DTC a no-action letter allowing it to tokenize Russell 1000 stocks, major index ETFs and U.S. Treasuries. DTCC has also worked with Chainlink on tokenized collateral management and laid out its plans for the service earlier this year as major Wall Street firms signed on.

The bank-led approach contrasts with crypto-native efforts to tokenize stocks. Fifty-six companies, including Tesla, SpaceX, Amazon, and Nvidia, have objected to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, a planned tokenized stock venue from OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, those objections bar the venue from listing third-party tokenized versions of their stock.

Demand is building, but the market is still young. The International Monetary Fund found last month that tokenized stocks trade mostly outside U.S. market hours, though they remain more volatile and less liquid than their traditional counterparts.

Washington, D.C., November 6, 2026 — The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA), a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing clear and ethical public policy, research, and education related to emerging technologies, participated in the Strobe Summit, where DSA Managing Director Adrian Wall moderated a fireside chat with former Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Christiopher  Giancarlo on the evolving regulatory landscape for digital assets and the future of financial markets.

Wall and Giancarlo also examined the regulatory challenges surrounding prediction markets, perpetual futures, and decentralized finance (DeFi). Topics included the CFTC’s role in overseeing event contracts, bringing offshore derivatives activity into regulated U.S. markets, the potential for 24/7 trading, and establishing accountability for decentralized platforms without traditional intermediaries. The discussion highlighted the need for regulatory frameworks that address market integrity, cybersecurity, customer asset protection, and the operational realities of increasingly interconnected financial markets.

DSA’s participation reflects its commitment to advancing informed policy dialogue and practical regulatory approaches that support responsible innovation, market integrity, and the integration of digital assets into the broader financial system.

#5254. Zcash (ZEC) OI Down 7.8% as NU7 Upgrade Goes Live

Zcash open interest has declined 7.8%, according to the data from analytical platform Coinglass.

Open interest (OI) refers to the value of futures contracts that are still open. In other words, the rise in OI means more active positions.

When a price and OI decline simultaneously, it usually suggests deleveraging. The traders might be closing positions or their positions might be liquidated.

ZEC is trading near $1,286, down 1.5% over the past 24 hours. The price’s pullback comes amid a broader market correction, with BTC down 5.75% in 24 hours.

Zcash gained 7.69% on November 4, rising on high expectations surrounding NU7. The upgrade introduces several changes to the network's transaction processing and reward structure.

As the upgrade went live on November 5, the target block interval went from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. According to the project’s statement, the change makes private payments confirm three times faster.

In addition to that, NU7 introduces a new transaction fee allocation model. 60% of the fees will go directly to a reserve for future network reserves, while the miners receive the remaining 40%.

Other changes include increased capacity for the Orchard shielded pool and new limits for wallet protection from spam.

So far, the market response has been mixed amid Friday’s correction. However, the ZEC chart is currently showing signs of an uptrend.

The price is testing support around $1,250, a level that could influence its next move. A sustained recovery above the $1,260-1,275 corridor would stabilize the further rebound.

On the other hand, a break below $1,230 would mean a failed recovery and a prolonged downtrend.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Bloodbath is the perfect word to describe the post-election market action.

Despite the markets trading on the assumption that Democrats will win, with odds hitting a high of 99%, crypto has suffered a severe sell-off. However, the downside may not be over yet. The total crypto market cap has now slipped back to mid-September levels, marking five straight weeks of losses and wiping out nearly $900 billion in market value.

The result? A textbook liquidity sweep. According to Coinglass, nearly $1 billion in positions were liquidated on the 5th of September, marking the largest single-day wipeout since the $2 billion short squeeze in mid-August. However, unlike that event, nearly 80% of the liquidations came from longs, showing that bullish traders were heavily caught offside as the market moved lower.

That said, the sell-off wasn’t just “crypto-specific.”

As the chart above shows, the Nasdaq 100 suffered its largest one-day loss since the pandemic, while the S&P500 lost $3 trillion in value. This comes just 24 hours after the Dow surged 1,600 points after Democrats swept the midterms. This indicates that there has been an abrupt change in sentiment post-election.

Notably, the U.S. President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to say that it is one of the stock market’s “worst days in history.” The crypto wipeout seems to be part of a wider correction in the market, with post-election volatility adding to the selling pressure. However, the move may not be just another election-driven pullback. The latest market data suggests there could be more going on beneath the surface.

The market FUD seems to be less about the election itself and more about President Trump.

From a technical standpoint, this shift in sentiment makes sense. Crypto initially saw a strong boost from optimism around his election, but that momentum has since faded. However, the momentum has died out. Bitcoin [BTC] is currently down almost 30% from its peak of $126k despite progress made in regulation with the GENIUS Act, greater tokenization and increased adoption in stablecoins into traditional finance.

To add to the pressure, there are now reports that Trump Media sold a total of $343 million worth of Bitcoin. This adds to concerns regarding institutional selling and has also created more FUD around Trump, further weakening the bullish sentiment that initially drove crypto’s post-election rally.

Against this backdrop, crypto’s wipeout could be more than just a reaction to broader market weakness.

Besides the traditional markets digesting how the election will affect the AI space, there are further pressures on the crypto space. #5252. HBAR’s 88% Slide Leaves It Ahead of Most 2021 Rivals

Home » Trendsetter News » HBAR’s 88% Slide Leaves It Ahead of Most 2021 Rivals

A larger token supply complicates any recovery, making a return to its former price a much bigger valuation hurdle.

HBAR remains roughly 88% below its record price, yet the analyst in a recent video places it closer to recovery than most of the largest cryptocurrencies from 2021. That comparison is less a sign of strength than a measure of how severely much of that market has fallen.

Using CoinMarketCap’s November 7, 2021 rankings, the analyst selected the 50 largest coins after excluding stablecoins and wrapped assets. In the video’s snapshot, 41 remained at least 80% below their respective highs, with the median decline around 97%.

“It’s not a forecast,” Cheeky Crypto says. The figures describe historical performance, not the likelihood of a recovery.

At the roughly $0.07 price cited in the video, HBAR would need to rise about eightfold to revisit its approximately $0.57 intraday peak. The analyst separates that brief high from its strongest daily close, just above $0.50 on Binance in September 2021.

The proposed recovery levels start at $0.10, about 43% above the video’s reference price. Next comes $0.25, roughly 3.6 times that price, followed by the record itself.

HBAR has already demonstrated that a substantial rally need not restore earlier buyers’ losses.

Its strongest daily close since 2021 was around $0.37 in January 2025, according to the video, still roughly a quarter below its record close despite an approximately tenfold rise from late 2022.

The bigger obstacle is supply. Cheeky Crypto says the amount of HBAR released from treasury has more than tripled since its record, making a return to $0.57 a materially different valuation proposition.

At the supply level cited, that price would imply a market capitalization near $25 billion. Matching HBAR’s historical peak market capitalization would instead require roughly $0.11 to $0.16 per token, depending on the historical supply figures used.

That valuation is not equivalent to cash that must enter the market, a distinction the analyst explicitly makes. But additional token releases could raise the valuation required to regain the old price.

For investors, the useful distinction is between recovering a token price and recovering a network valuation. HBAR’s smaller drawdown relative to many peers does not erase dilution or make its former high an inevitable destination.

#5251. BSC Releases Reth Exploit Hotfix: Details About the Upgrade

BNB Smart Chain (BSC) has released a hotfix to its Reth execution client, BSC-Reth, according to the official announcement and a patch on Github. The patch addresses a vulnerability discovered on November 4, 2026, which could result in incorrect blockchain state-root calculations due to a bug in the legacy trie code (used to organize blockchain data).

Although the vulnerability could have resulted in financial loss, there is no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited or that funds were affected.

Rust Ethereum Harvester Tree, also known as Reth, is an execution client used to verify the data on the blockchain and process transactions. On November 4, 2026, a vulnerability was discovered in certain versions of Reth that could result in incorrect state-root calculations due to a bug in the legacy trie code.

This could potentially result in node disagreements and sync failures. The underlying bug was fixed in Reth pull request #28264, merged on November 3.

On November 6, BNB Chain published BSC-Reth v0.1.4-hotfix on GitHub. According to the release notes, this version includes a fix for incorrect state-root calculation in the legacy path in Reth. This version of BSC-Reth improves the way it deals with blockchain data, reducing the risk of incorrect state-root calculation during state verification.

All BSC-Reth node operators, including validators, MEV builders, full nodes, and sentry nodes, are advised to upgrade to this version and restart the node as soon as possible. This fix does not require a DB migration or hard fork. Users do not need to take any action. BNB Chain has also confirmed that this vulnerability has a limited effect on BSC-Reth and has no effect on opBNB.

#5250. Treasury bought back $6B in bonds, but dealers say bigger isn’t enough

Treasury's latest $6 billion buyback shows why Wall Street dealers want the government to rethink how it buys bonds, not just how much it buys.

The US Treasury bought back $6 billion of older government bonds on Nov. 4, hitting the full limit of its latest operation. On paper, that looks like a success for a program designed to make the Treasury market easier to trade.

But there's a catch. One bond accounted for $4.9 billion, or 82% of everything Treasury agreed to buy. Add another $950 million from a second bond, and just two securities made up almost 98% of the entire purchase. Of the 40 bonds eligible for the operation, only seven were bought.

This is the kind of concentration Wall Street dealers have been worried about for months. In feedback published by Treasury on Nov. 4, dealers said the larger buybacks were helping market liquidity.

However, they also explained why simply increasing the program size might not be enough to achieve that.

Their feedback came before Wednesday's operation, so they weren't responding to this particular result. We now know the Treasury can buy billions of dollars of bonds and still leave dealers holding the securities they hoped to sell. The amount purchased is important, but so is how those purchases are spread around.

The Treasury market is enormous, but not every government bond trades equally easily. The newest issues attract the most attention and typically have the deepest markets. Older bonds, known as off-the-run Treasuries, can be harder to sell quickly without accepting a lower price.

That's where dealers come in. They buy bonds from customers, keep them on their books, and look for someone else willing to take them.

But holding those bonds costs money, sometimes a lot of money. That's why dealers often have to borrow to finance their positions, exposing them to price changes while they wait for another buyer. The longer they hold a bond, the more those costs and risks compound.

Treasury's liquidity-support buybacks give them another potential buyer: the government itself.

In September, Treasury began larger buybacks of longer-dated bonds, at least doubling the previous $2 billion maximum for those operations. The idea was to provide a more reliable outlet for older securities.

According to the Nov. 4 dealer feedback, most dealers reported at least modest improvements. They said the purchases had made it easier to find an exit for older bonds, reduced the risk of sudden price distortions, and helped keep pricing relationships between similar securities more stable.

While that's meaningful progress, the Treasury got mixed answers when it asked whether the changes had improved dealers' ability to handle customer trades.

A lack of unity among dealers is what makes these buybacks so controversial. We now have dealers that welcome a large government buyer but aren't necessarily becoming more willing to buy bonds from customers.

If the Treasury keeps concentrating its purchases in a handful of issues, dealers holding other, older issues still have to find other buyers or keep financing the position. In other words, the buyback program can work without working equally well across the entire market.

Dealers wanted better, earlier communication about operations, smaller purchases more frequently, and limits that would help distribute Treasury buying across a wider range of individual securities.

More frequent operations would give dealers more opportunities to sell, as they'd get another chance sooner.

Limits on how much of one security the Treasury can buy could also prevent a single bond from absorbing most of the available capacity. Each bond has its own identifying number, called a CUSIP, so dealers suggested using per-CUSIP limits to spread purchases more broadly.

Some dealers specifically warned about the risk of missing a concentrated buyback and being left to manage the interest-rate exposure from bonds that remained on their books.

This is exactly what we saw on Wednesday. According to the official data, Treasury received $39.6 billion in offers for an operation capped at $6 billion. That means dealers and other eligible participants offered more than six times what Treasury ultimately accepted.

And despite that demand, one bond maturing in November 2041 absorbed more than 80% of the purchases.

Nov. 4, 2026 operation, accepted face value in USD. Labels identify coupon and maturity. All seven purchased securities are shown; 40 were eligible. Eligibility does not show which unpurchased issues were offered. Face value is not cash expenditure. The largest share is calculated as $4.924 billion / $6 billion. Settlement: Nov. 5.

Source: U.S. Treasury: Nov. 4 buyback result, pages 1–2

It's worth being careful about what those numbers tell us. Treasury doesn't publish the full breakdown of rejected offers, so we don't know whether every one of the 33 eligible bonds that received no purchases was actually offered. We also can't assume Treasury made a bad decision by concentrating its buying.

This is because buybacks are extremely competitive operations. Treasury evaluates the prices offered and the relative value of the securities, so if one bond presents particularly attractive offers, buying more of it may make sense for taxpayers.

The problem is that getting the best available prices and helping the widest range of sellers aren't necessarily the same thing.

Nov. 4, 2026 operation, USD face value. Treasury accepted $6 billion against $39.636 billion offered, filling the $6 billion maximum. These overlapping measures are compared, not added. The offer ratio is 39.636 / 6 = 6.606, rounded to 6.61. Offered face value does not count distinct sellers or unique inventory. Filling the maximum is not a measured liquidity improvement.

Source: U.S. Treasury: Nov. 4 buyback result, operation totals

Treasury also has existing limits designed to preserve the amount of individual securities circulating in the market. Dealers are asking for changes that could distribute purchases more evenly within those constraints.

They discussed other possibilities, including alternative pricing methods and transactions that would exchange one security for another. But those would be more complicated to introduce, and Treasury said they would require further work.

For now, the most immediate requests are simpler: communicate earlier, buy more often, and avoid having so much of the operation go to just one security.

For investors watching Treasury buybacks as a potential source of liquidity for Bitcoin, a $6 billion buyback doesn't automatically mean $6 billion in fresh liquidity is headed toward risk assets.

First, the $6 billion is the face value of the debt Treasury agreed to retire. Because those bonds were trading below face value, the cash purchase amount was approximately $4 billion before accrued interest.

Second, Treasury continues issuing new debt to finance the government even as it buys back older securities.

So the program primarily changes which bonds are outstanding and how easily dealers can manage them. It doesn't automatically increase the amount of money available to buy Bitcoin.

However, a connection may still exist through financial conditions. An Oct. 30 Federal Reserve study, using data through June 2025, found that Treasury buybacks reduced dealers' bond inventories and eased some risk constraints for trading desks.

But the researchers found no statistically significant reduction in dealers' repo activity.

Repo is essentially short-term borrowing backed by securities. It's one way dealers and their customers finance bond positions. That's important because taking bonds off dealers' books doesn't necessarily eliminate the financing demands tied to the broader market.

For Bitcoin to benefit, easier Treasury trading would need to translate into better financing conditions or greater investor capacity to take risk. Wednesday's purchase result alone can't tell us whether that happened.

The next question is whether Treasury changes the program in ways that make those improvements more consistent.

In its latest quarterly plan, Treasury said it anticipates up to $70 billion in liquidity-support buybacks from November through January, alongside a separate $25 billion for cash management purposes. It also confirmed that it's evaluating changes to purchase limits, scheduling, frequency, eligibility, and execution.

That gives dealers a chance to see whether their feedback leads to something concrete.

The real market test won't be whether Treasury manages to spend its full buyback allowance. It'll be whether more bonds become easier to trade, dealers become more willing to handle customer orders, and financing pressures actually ease.

A $6 billion buyback might look impressive on paper, but for a dealer still holding a bond nobody wants to buy, the announcement's size only goes so far.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. A joint operation of the People's Bank of China with Shanghai police clamped down on the Solana Accelerate China 2026 four-day tour. Authorities blocked the project's events in Shanghai, while the financial regulator in parallel launched an investigation against those locals who helped the blockchain platform with logistics and public relations.

What drew such a harsh reaction from the Chinese authorities was 'too aggressive' offline marketing of the tour. On the evening of October 14, a team associated with Solana, together with Shanghai contractors, put giant vibrant logos of the SOL token on the Citigroup Tower skyscraper facade in Lujiazui - the very heart of Shanghai's financial district. This was not just an ad: top managers, including Solana Foundation president Lily Lu, started publicly boasting about the opening of Shanghai's new office in a prestigious building.

All this massive campaign predictably caused an excitement in crypto circles. Even Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, known simply as CZ, expressed his amusement, calling 'amazing' the fact that Solana managed to not only do a promo in China, but get an office there as well. BNB Chain did not achieve such a success, added CZ.

It seems like the organizers tried to bypass the regulatory barriers using a positioning trick. The four-day tour between Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, and Beijing was marketed strictly around technologies like AI agents, robots, IT development - not about crypto at all.

The maneuver did not get recognition in China to say the least, and the backlash did not take long to follow.

The morning session on October 16 in Shangri-La was shut down outright, with participants held for over an hour on the street after police suddenly arrived. Lily Lu tried to narrow the angles and stated that the cancellation was caused by registrations quadrupling, so the site was not ready to invite all registrants.

Fast forward to November 6 and representatives of the People's Bank of China, in an exclusive interview with the state agency Financial News, finally ended speculations on what actually happened. He directly called the skyline ad and all the aligned events an illegal marketing of virtual currencies. The Central Bank's position is 'black and white' there: SOL is a cryptocurrency and Solana's infra not only facilitates coins issuance, but also helps stablecoin turnover (especially USDT), which is banned.

Organizers in the face of Solana Foundation breached the crypto-risk agreement jointly issued back in February 2026 by eight Chinese authority departments. The document directly bans all the promotion of overseas crypto projects and implements individual liability for Chinese citizens and companies that help to do this.

Solana Foundation hasn't provided any official comments on the matter yet.

The signal by People's Bank of China is unambiguous though: full cleanup of all the mainland market out of foreign blockchain networks and activities associated with them.

#5247. Bitcoin Rebounds After Democratic Midterm Sweep, But Crypto Faces Tougher Fight in Washington

Bitcoin Rebounds After Democratic Midterm Sweep, But Crypto Faces Tougher Fight in Washington

Bitcoin and Ethereum recovered Wednesday after Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, despite the results likely making the crypto industry's push for friendlier federal rules more difficult.

The crypto market recovery, in technical terms, appears to be more a natural bounce, and in line with expectations, instead of a trend reversal or a FOMO-driven spike. The overnight selloff also reversed as U.S. stock futures bounced back, making it hard to pin the recovery on politics alone.

Bitcoin briefly hit a six-week low before a bounce that took it back to just above $80,000 once again, above its average price of the last 50 days, which is a solid bullish sign after weeks of bearish correction.

Ethereum, meanwhile, spiked 7% to $2,434, while U.S. stocks on the whole jumped around 1.6%, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average leading the way with a 2.5% rally.

Analysts who spoke to Decrypt said the Democratic sweep had largely been priced into crypto markets before election night. A rebound in Bitcoin therefore says less about investors welcoming the election result than about how much bad news they were already expecting.

The industry has spent more than $300 million supporting crypto-friendly candidates from both parties across the 2024 and 2026 election cycles. About $176 million went toward more than 100 races this year alone.

That spending was aimed partly at getting legislation through Congress that would give digital asset businesses clearer rules. The Clarity Act, a major piece of that effort, would define how federal regulators oversee different types of crypto assets and trading activity.

The bill was in trouble before Tuesday's election. Senators voted 49-50 against advancing it in September, falling short of the 60 votes needed to move past a procedural hurdle. That was not a final vote on the legislation, but it stopped the measure from reaching a full debate.

Negotiations had already run into disputes over restrictions on government officials' crypto business interests and the treatment of rewards paid on stablecoins, tokens designed to hold a fixed value. President Donald Trump's personal and family crypto ventures became a particular point of conflict for Democratic lawmakers.

Democratic control of Congress makes a quick return to the same legislative deal less likely, but it does not automatically undo what the industry secured under Trump. His administration has eased enforcement, established a strategic Bitcoin reserve and overseen the passage of a federal stablecoin law.

The distinction matters more for exchanges, token issuers, and other firms seeking clear legal permissions than for Bitcoin's day-to-day price. Analysts told Decrypt that liquidity, interest rates and investment flows still exert a stronger influence on the cryptocurrency itself.

The broader crypto market has shed roughly $300 billion over the past month, bringing its total value to about $2.67 trillion. Rising borrowing costs and worries about returns on artificial intelligence investments have pushed traders toward less risky assets like bonds or gold.

Major Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which offer exposure to the asset through traditional brokerage accounts, recorded $215 million in net withdrawals in October. That brought their year-to-date net outflows to $1.84 billion.

The new Congress takes office in January 2027. Unless lawmakers revive the Clarity Act before the current session ends, the industry will need to start a new legislative effort with Democrats controlling both chambers.

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in Q1 2026 amid weaker Bitcoin prices, low mining profitability, and declining equipment values. It also recorded a $41.9 million loss after terminating mining equipment agreements with Block and Proto in Q2.

However, the latest netflow has settled back to a small positive reading of about 179.4 BTC, which suggests the miner selling pressure has cooled.

#5245. Gate boasts 104% cold reserve coverage, but separate snapshot dates raise red flags

Its new hot-wallet loss test uses separate measurement bases, while independent verification of current PoSEC data remains in progress.

Crypto exchange Gate has introduced Proof of Security, a disclosure framework that proves its cold assets cover customer balances if it lost all its hot-wallet assets.

Its Nov. 5 announcement reports 104.58% cold-storage coverage, using a storage snapshot taken at 00:00 UTC on Nov. 4.

The published percentage compares asset shares from different snapshots, rather than establishing cold assets and customer balances on a single common date. Gate discloses that limitation, so customers need more than the headline ratio to verify the full-backing claim.

Gate's PoSEC methodology compares an 88.26% cold-storage share with an 84.39% user-asset share. The remaining shares are 11.74% in hot wallets and 15.61% owned by the platform.

Cold storage is measured against cold assets plus hot-wallet assets in the storage snapshot, while user assets are measured against platform reserves in the separate Proof of Reserves snapshot. The FAQ defines the coverage calculation as the first share divided by the second.

The page explicitly says the snapshots have different totals and that intervening price changes and fund movements are not reflected.

Same-date backing needs aligned balances. Gate’s reported percentage combines shares from different snapshot totals.

The reported 104.58% share comparison alone cannot establish backing at one common date.

Different snapshot dates and totals; intervening price changes and fund movements are excluded. The earlier PoR reference is not separately dated in the chart. This does not establish insolvency or losses.

Rings normalize each reported share to its own 100% total; they do not compare absolute dollar values. Arc lengths use the displayed percentages. 88.26+11.74=100 and 84.39+15.61=100. The 104.58% result is Gate-reported, not recomputed from rounded display inputs.

Different snapshot dates and totals; intervening price changes and fund movements are excluded. The earlier PoR reference is not separately dated in the chart. This does not establish insolvency or losses.

Gate's Oct. 21 disclosure reports roughly $8.7 billion in reserves and $7.3 billion in user net assets as of Oct. 18, with a 118.49% overall reserve ratio.

The PoSEC chart does not separately date its earlier user-asset reference, and the October dollar totals cannot be combined with November storage percentages to present a measured dollar buffer.

A direct test of backing after a hot-wallet loss would compare surviving cold assets with customer balances at the same time, using compatible valuations and the same reporting perimeter.

The disclosure leaves a gap in demonstrating common-date coverage, as it doesn't establish either insolvency or customer losses.

Gate's definition includes digital assets in cold wallets and traditional assets, such as stocks and US Treasuries, held by independent custodians.

The exchange says qualifying assets must sit outside routine deposit and withdrawal operations, be offline or independently custodied, require multiparty transfer authorization, and be verifiable. It also explains that off-chain traditional assets can make reported cold storage exceed balances visible in blockchain cold wallets.

As of Nov. 5, the PoSEC page lists independent third-party verification as in progress. Gate says the review covers asset authenticity and control, valuation and reporting scope, and the coverage calculation.

Gate's PoSEC FAQ says individual wallet addresses are currently withheld for security reasons, making the promised independent report particularly relevant to public scrutiny.

That review should be distinguished from the older audit shown on Gate's Proof of Reserves page. The page dates a Hacken implementation assessment to Jan. 3, 2024. Hacken describes that work as examining code, architecture, build processes, and vulnerabilities.

The new framework gives customers a concrete scenario to evaluate. The decisive next evidence is a common-date reconciliation of cold assets and customer balances, with valuation methods, entity scope, custody restrictions, and asset composition clear enough to assess the claim.

A completed review can show how those pieces fit together, while a comparison of percentages from different snapshots cannot do that by itself.

#5244. Paraguay Bank-Freeze Puts XRP Custody Risk in Focus

Home » Trendsetter News » Paraguay Bank-Freeze Puts XRP Custody Risk in Focus

A mass bank-account freeze in Paraguay have renewed discussion of XRP and self-custody.

More than 3 million people locked out of their bank accounts overnight: that is the claim driving a video by Edo Farina, a popular researcher covering banks and crypto. He alleges that Paraguay’s central bank took control of digital bank Ueno, using the purported disruption to argue for XRP and self-custody.

Edo Farina’s central comparison is between allegedly inaccessible bank deposits and the XRP Ledger continuing to process transactions. “The XRP Ledger kept settling transactions every few seconds like any other day,” he says.

That distinction concerns network availability, not investment performance. In the same video, he puts XRP near $1.25, down roughly 5%, and bitcoin below $77,000, also falling nearly 5%. These are figures quoted during the recording, not current market prices.

He identifies $1.60 as XRP’s key resistance level and says he would not call a reversal before it is reclaimed.

His broader argument that banking failures will increase demand for XRP as a settlement asset is a forecast; continued ledger operation alone does not demonstrate increased adoption or demand.

The YouTube video’s practical emphasis is on spreading exposure across banks, keeping emergency cash and holding cryptocurrency keys outside exchanges. Exchange-held assets can become inaccessible through platform restrictions, insolvency proceedings or legal action.

But Edo overstates the protection when he says nobody can seize XRP held with personal keys. Native XRP has no issuer clawback mechanism; the ledger does support clawback for certain issued tokens. Neither distinction makes an owner immune to legal orders, stolen keys or compelled transfers.

His claim that physical property cannot be confiscated is similarly too broad. Gold and real estate remain subject to seizure under applicable law.

Holding keys removes reliance on an exchange to authorize transfers, but it does not protect XRP’s market value or make an unverified banking story evidence of its future demand.

#5243. Optimism new proposal weakens council power over standalone chains

The proposed policy would let qualifying transfers proceed without another governance vote, changing who users rely on for upgrades.

An Optimism governance proposal published Nov. 5 would require at least 30 days' public notice before a chain transfers upgrade control from the shared Security Council, giving users time to assess changes to the network's security model.

The proposed Standard Rollup Charter amendment concerns chains whose upgrade authority rests with the Council under the Charter. It would let a Chain Governor request that control move to an address of its choosing, so it could manage upgrades itself or through a third party.

A completed transfer would mean relying on the security model of the new upgrade key holder. Optimism Governance and the Security Council would no longer retain the same practical ability to enforce the Charter's policies on that chain through upgrade authority.

The policy's accompanying GitHub amendment PR 74 was still open on Nov. 5 and says it will merge only if governance accepts the proposal.

A governor would first submit a request to the Optimism Foundation, which would confirm that it is valid and complies with the governor's commitments. The Foundation would then publish notice on the Governance Forum.

That notice should identify the chain, its Chain ID, and material layer-1 contract addresses. It should also warn that the chain would cease to be a Standard Rollup if the transfer goes ahead.

The Security Council would have to wait at least 30 days from publication before executing the transaction. The proposed policy says the Council should check that the Foundation published the notice, that the minimum period has elapsed, and that the recipient address matches the one the Foundation supplied on the governor's behalf.

A transfer meeting the approved policy's conditions would need no additional Optimism Governance approval. That would remove the need to seek a separate vote for each handover.

#5242. Tech, AI Stocks Split After Democratic Sweep: Microsoft Jumps, Tesla and Nvidia Tank

Tech, AI Stocks Split After Democratic Sweep: Microsoft Jumps, Tesla and Nvidia Tank

Technology stocks delivered a mixed performance Wednesday after Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections, with investors weighing the prospect of tougher artificial intelligence regulation against expectations that a divided government could limit major policy changes.

The Nasdaq-100 climbed 1.14% to 28,500, recovering from an overnight selloff that briefly pushed index futures down more than 2%.

But beneath the broader market rebound, individual technology stocks told sharply different stories.

Microsoft jumped 6.01% to $552.32, while Google parent Alphabet rose 4.63% to $292.99, according to intraday charts reviewed Wednesday.

While software stocks jumped, hardware stocks corrected to the downside. AI chipmaking giant Nvidia fell 2.19% to $202.17, Tesla dropped 3.61% to $384.10, and Intel lost 5.80% to $57.04.

That said, none has yet shown a heavy bearish trend. Even Nvidia, which is going through the most obvious price correction, remains bullish on the longer trend as the prices test a weak support near the $200 price zone.

Bitcoin also recovered strongly, trading around $80,512, up 4.12% in the day, after an initial election-related selloff.

The conflicting moves reflect the uncertainty over what Democratic control of Congress will mean for technology companies that have benefited from the Donald Trump administration's approach to deregulation.

According to Reuters, investors are particularly concerned about greater scrutiny of AI data centers—the hardware camps of the AI industry—following Democratic victories in states such as Texas and Georgia, where large infrastructure projects have become politically contentious.

The AI sector was already facing questions over enormous infrastructure spending and whether those investments would generate adequate returns.

One of Wednesday's biggest losers was Trump Media & Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social.

Shares plunged 14.29% to $5.10, extending a decline that had been underway long before Democrats secured control of Congress.

The stock had already lost approximately 55% of its value year-to-date before Tuesday's vote.

Technical indicators show traders had been bearish on the stock for months. Trump Media has been in a technical pattern that traders refer to as a “death cross” since March 2025, and has lost nearly 90% of its market cap since its 2024 cap. A death cross happens when the average price of the last 200 days becomes greater than that of the last 50 days, suggesting the asset is losing value way too quickly.

The Nasdaq-100's recovery is encouraging for technology bulls, but the index remains well below its October highs above 31,000. The 28,000 area represents an immediate support zone, while a move back above 29,000 would strengthen the short-term recovery.

Bitcoin's recovery above $80,000 offers another indication that risk appetite has not disappeared entirely.

Still, Wednesday's split between technology winners and losers suggests investors are becoming increasingly selective about their exposure to the AI boom—and the political risks surrounding it.

#5239. Ukraine Central Bank Refuses to Back Crypto Bill Cleared for Second Reading

Ukraine's National Bank says draft law 10225-d on virtual assets lacks safeguards on foreign tokens and platform licensing.

Ukraine’s central bank will not support a crypto market bill that a parliamentary committee cleared for a final vote, warning that the draft leaves foreign tokens that act like electronic money outside its control and risks monetary sovereignty.

The National Bank of Ukraine said in a Nov. 4 statement that Draft Law No. 10225-d on the circulation of virtual assets, recommended by the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Finance, Tax and Customs Policy for adoption in the second reading and as a whole, fails to reflect compromises struck during drafting.

The NBU said it received the final text only late the evening before the committee vote and that the process “was not sufficiently transparent.” Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban raised the bank’s objections at the committee meeting, but the NBU said the format did not allow a full debate.

Ukraine already legalized a framework for virtual assets in 2022. The new bill is meant to put that market under detailed rules modeled on the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or MiCA, and on International Monetary Fund recommendations. The NBU says it supports that direction in principle.

The bank’s public case rests on three points.

First, the draft would let foreign tokens into Ukraine even when they function as electronic money but face no matching supervision in the countries where they are issued. That, the NBU said, threatens monetary sovereignty, the transmission of monetary policy, payment infrastructure and financial stability.

The bank wants the same power it has over domestically issued tokens: the authority to assess those foreign assets and, when needed, restrict their circulation in Ukraine.

Second, simplified admission of foreign virtual assets must not let them sidestep rules that apply to comparable Ukrainian assets. Without that parity, the NBU warned, segments of the market could expand outside adequate oversight and create regulatory arbitrage.

Third, the bank flagged monopolization and corruption risks in how the National Securities and Stock Market Commission would authorize trading-platform operators. The NBU initially opposed numerical caps, then agreed as a compromise to limit the first wave to three legal persons chosen by competitive selection.

The final draft, it said, drops a clear five-year cap and leaves the number of operators to the securities commission’s discretion without enough antitrust safeguards.

The committee’s Nov. 4 recommendation does not enact the law. A final Verkhovna Rada vote is expected later in November. If adopted, the rules would take effect on July 1, 2027, Interfax Ukraine reported, splitting supervision between the NBU and the securities commission.

Under the committee version, personal income from virtual-asset trades would face Ukraine’s standard personal income tax, with a reduced 5% rate through the end of 2028 for assets acquired before the law takes effect. Crypto-to-crypto exchanges would not be taxed, and virtual-asset deals would sit outside VAT.

The fight lands as Ukraine continues to debate how deep bitcoin and other digital assets should sit in state finance. Lawmakers last year introduced a separate bill that would let the NBU hold virtual assets, including bitcoin, in its foreign-exchange and gold reserves, a permission the bank would not be required to use.

“The development of the virtual asset market and the protection of monetary and financial stability are not mutually exclusive,” the NBU said. It called on members of parliament to refine the document with all parties to the process and said it remains ready to cooperate.

The test now is whether Ukraine’s lawmakers reopen the foreign-token and licensing clauses before a floor vote, or push the committee text through and leave the central bank on the outside of a framework it helped draft.

#5238. Unpatched Bitcoin Lightning nodes face channel-draining bug

Core Lightning urges Bitcoin node operators to patch payment and channel security flaws and tighten remote-access credentials.

Core Lightning, software for operating Bitcoin Lightning payment nodes, is urging users to install v26.06.10 to address channel-security, payment-resolution, and remote-access flaws.

Maintainers also recommend reviewing the credentials used for remote commands, making access restrictions a separate task alongside the software upgrade.

The release notice recommends upgrading as soon as practical. Maintainers have temporarily withheld security-fix tests to slow the conversion of patches into working exploits and give operators more time to upgrade.

The new version adds checks on a peer's transaction signatures during Bitcoin dual-funded channel opening and splicing, following the Lightning protocol's BOLT 2 specification, according to the tagged changelog.

A conditional Bitcoin payment contract, known as an HTLC, that had just been removed could be confused with a live one sharing its payment hash, amount and expiry. The node could then fail the live payment upstream even though its peer could still claim it.

Another fix rejects channel opens when a peer proposes a dust limit above 5,000 satoshis. The changelog says the previous behavior let a peer trim the node's balance into fees during a forced close. Dual-funded opens also reject a peer's dust limit when it exceeds the channel reserve.

Dual funding remains experimental, and maintainers discourage zero-confirmation channels with untrusted peers. The release also refuses a v2 zero-confirmation open unless the operator has configured acceptance for that peer.

Nodes that have run master cannot downgrade into the 26.06.x series because their database schema is newer.

GitHub displays a Nov. 4 release date for v26.06.10, while its tagged changelog dates the same version Nov. 5. The release follows the v26.06.9 security fixes and the Nov. 2 separate stored-trigger crash.

Core Lightning's commando interface lets a directly connected peer request that a node execute a command. The peer generally needs a rune, an authorization credential permitting the command.

The update closes a way to bypass rune restrictions on parameter names using duplicate or punctuation-variant names. It also fixes a commando crash triggered by reusing a command ID after a failed command and rejects oversized runes that previously consumed excessive decoding work.

Maintainers recommend binding runes used over commando to the application's node ID through a id restriction. They also advise operators to blacklist runes they cannot account for using blacklistrune, then issue replacements with tighter restrictions.
